record.title: SkelWAM reports cross-embodiment manipulation transfer from one source robot
record.summary: The authors introduce SkelWAM, which maps whole-body geometry, tool pose and gripper state into a shared 25-dimensional action representation. In the author-reported LIBERO-Cross10 simulation benchmark, it reached 43.3% success across 1,000 paired episodes on ten tasks and ten target embodiments (95% Wilson interval 40.3–46.4%), compared with 7.1% for the strongest evaluated baseline, RoVi-Aug with a Fast-WAM backbone and target-specific end-effector inverse kinematics. Task results varied substantially: success was higher on Cross-Spatial/Cross-Object (61.3%/61.0%) than Cross-Goal/Cross-Long (15.0%/18.0%). A separate JAKA mini2-to-Feagine A03 physical study describes three tasks qualitatively and reports no physical success rate or trial count in the inspected text. The authors permit task-independent target calibration, and baseline pretraining/adaptation budgets differ.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that SkelWAM uses a shared 25-dimensional representation of arm centerline geometry, tool-center-point pose and parallel-jaw commands, with embodiment-specific decoders, and does not use target-task demonstrations or target-policy updates.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On LIBERO-Cross10, the authors report 43.3% success over 1,000 paired episodes (95% Wilson interval 40.3–46.4%), compared with 7.1% for RoVi-Aug with a Fast-WAM backbone and target-specific end-effector inverse kinematics, the strongest evaluated baseline. Each method is evaluated on the same ten target embodiments, ten tasks and ten paired trial indices per cell; target-independent calibration is allowed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a deployment of a JAKA mini2-trained policy on a Feagine A03 continuum robot for three tabletop manipulation tasks.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected source does not establish independent reproduction, performance across broader task distributions, or the amount of physical validation beyond the three reported tabletop tasks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report higher average success on Cross-Spatial and Cross-Object (61.3% and 61.0%) than on Cross-Goal and Cross-Long (15.0% and 18.0%); the physical Feagine A03 deployment is presented qualitatively without a reported trial count or success rate.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper tables and protocol were inspected, but the linked project site could not be retrieved and no independent reproduction or code execution was performed.
The physical deployment section describes three tasks but gives no physical trial counts, task success rate or uncertainty estimate.

brief.importance_rationale: If the central transfer claim holds across the stated robot morphologies, one source embodiment could support manipulation on multiple target bodies without target demonstrations, reducing a recurring data and integration bottleneck. The reported physical evidence is a limited three-task demonstration and the benchmark result has not been independently reproduced, so its current consequence is meaningful rather than field-shifting.
limitations: All performance numbers are reported by the paper authors; this review did not execute code or independently reproduce them.

The benchmark comprises ten selected LIBERO tasks and ten target embodiments, with Franka Panda as the sole source robot; source data include 467 successful demonstrations, and policy selection uses held-out source episodes.
The 43.3% aggregate hides substantial task-family variation: 61.3%/61.0% on Cross-Spatial/Cross-Object versus 15.0%/18.0% on Cross-Goal/Cross-Long.

Each method uses the same target/task trial indices, but VLA and WAM baselines use released checkpoints, adaptation budgets differ, and no baseline receives SkelWAM’s skeleton representation or body-tracking objective.
Evaluation permits task-independent target calibration, so “zero-shot” means no target-task demonstrations or target policy updates, not no target setup or calibration.
The physical JAKA mini2-to-Feagine A03 study covers three tabletop tasks and is qualitative in the inspected report; physical trial counts and success rates are not reported there.
The linked project site could not be retrieved during this review; code execution and independent artifact verification remain open.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 43.3% mean success over 1,000 paired episodes (95% Wilson interval 40.3–46.4%), versus 7.1% for RoVi-Aug with Fast-WAM and target-specific EEF-IK. Results vary by task family: 61.3%/61.0% on Cross-Spatial/Cross-Object and 15.0%/18.0% on Cross-Goal/Cross-Long. Zero-shot excludes target-task demonstrations and target-policy updates but permits task-independent target calibration.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary paper provides a detailed protocol and author-reported simulation tables. The same ten targets, ten tasks and ten paired trial indices per embodiment-task cell are used across methods; target/task coverage is comparable, but pretraining/adaptation budgets differ. The physical transfer is qualitative, without reported trial count or success rate. the research desk did not execute code or independently reproduce the results.
technical.mechanism: A shared skeleton-based state represents arm centerlines, tool-center-point pose and gripper commands; embodiment-specific constrained decoders map the representation to robot control actions.
technical.regime: Full paper reports ten selected LIBERO tasks, a Franka Panda source policy and ten target embodiments (nine rigid-link arms and one continuum arm), evaluated in MuJoCo/robosuite with 100 episodes per target (ten trials per task). Target-independent calibration is permitted. Baseline released-checkpoint pretraining/adaptation budgets differ. A separate physical study transfers JAKA mini2 source training to a Feagine A03 continuum robot on three tabletop tasks without target-task fine-tuning.
technical.reproducibility: The paper includes methods, task roster, per-target success table and a project-page link, but independent reproduction and code/artifact execution were not completed. The linked project site failed to load in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: RoVi-Aug adapted to a common Fast-WAM backbone, with target-specific end-effector inverse kinematics, reports 7.1% mean success against SkelWAM’s 43.3%. The target/task trial matrix is shared, but pretraining and source-adaptation budgets differ, and the baselines do not receive SkelWAM’s skeleton observations or body-tracking objective.

brief.title: SkelWAM reports cross-embodiment manipulation transfer from one source robot
brief.why_it_matters: If it transfers to other tasks and robots, a shared geometric action representation could reduce robot-specific data collection and integration. The paper reports a large simulation advantage under a matched target/task trial matrix, but baseline pretraining budgets differ, target calibration is allowed, performance varies sharply by task family, and the physical demonstration has no quantified success rate.
